texts.preamble: Bank Of Baroda vs Basanti Chaturvedi on 20 November, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Niharika Kumar Sharma, Senior Civil Judge -Cum-Rent Controller, Karkardooma Courts ,Shahdara Civ Suit 808/24 Unique Case Id No.DLSH03-001365-2024 Bank Of Baroda A body corporate duly constituted under The Banking Companies (Acquisition & Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970, Having its head office at:- Alkapuri, Vadodara-390007 With one of its Branches at:- 109, Shreshtha Vihar, Vigyan Vihar, Delhi-110092 E - mail: kardel@bankofbaroda.com Through its Principal Officer/Authorised Signatory Mr. Shambhu Kumar Jha, Chief Manager, Ec no.67102 Mob:8528428900. ...Plaintiff Vs. Basanti Chaturvedi, Prop. M/s. Hospitality 4 World Int., W/o Praveen Dutt, R-20, Office no.302, Pratap Complex, Shakarpur, Delhi-110092, Mob: 9891119407, 9868084927, 9718693999, E-mail: info@hospitality4world.com, basantichaturvedi@gmail.com. ...Defendant Suit for Recovery
texts.facts: The plaintiff is a body corporate constituted under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfers of Undertakings) Act, 1970, having its head office at Alkapuri, Vadodara 390007. The amalgamation of Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank with Bank of Baroda was santioned under the Bank of Baroda Scheme, 2019 dated 02.01.2019, issued by Government of India and published in Gazette of India, in terms of Section 9 of the said Act and Section 9 of Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfers of Undertakings) Act, 1980. All branches of Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank started functioning as branches of Bank of Baroda with effect from 01.04.2019. Mr. Shambhu Kumar Jha, Chief Managar, is the authorised signatory (AS) of the plaintiff bank in terms of the plaintiff bank's Board Resolution dated 14.11.2017. ii. The defendant approached Vijaya Bank for availing a cash credit facility of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) for her hospitality 4 world Int. of which the defendant was sole proprietor. In respect of the said loan, the plaintiff bank and the defendant vide certificate of loan papers DOC-54 dated 30.12.2016 entered into several agreements including Loan Agreement cum Hypothecation Deed DOC-53, Demand Promissory Note DOC-5 and undertaking DOC-35 all dated 30.12.2016. After availing the loan, defendant became irregular in making payment of monthly interest. The defendant acknowledged his liability towards the plaintiff bank vide acknowledgment of liability DOC-51 dated 31.08.2018 and letter of acknowledgment of debt dated 18.08.2021 of Rs. 48,310.87/- (Rupees Forty-Eight Thousand Three Hundred Ten and Eighty- Seven Paisa Only) and Rs.49,684.60/- (Rupees Forty-Nine Thousand Six Hundred Eighty-Four and Sixty Paisa Only). iv. The defendant, however, defaulted in making payments towards the stipulated EMIs and the loan account of the defendant became irregular and was declared as a NPA on 09.01.2023 as per applicable RBI guidelines. As per the statement of accounts of the defendant maintained by the plaintiff bank in the normal course of business, an amount of 58,692.78/- (Rupees Fifty-Eight Thousand Six Hundred Ninety Two and Sevety-Eight Paisa Only) inclusive of outstanding balance of Rs.47,818.10/-(Rupees Forty- Seven Thousand Eight Hundred Eighteen and Ten Paisa Only), unapplied interest of Rs. 7,887.18/-(Rupees Seven Thousand Eight Hundred Eighty-Seven and Eighteen Paisa Only), un- serviced interest of Rs.1,252.50/- (Rupees One Thousand Two Hundred Fifty-Two and Fifty Paisa Only) and compounding interest of Rs. 1,735.00/- (Rupees One Thousand Seven Hundred and Thirty-Five Only) is outstanding against the defendant as on 10.08.2024. 2. The summons of the present suit were issued to the defendant for service by way of ordinary process and registered post on 05.11.2024. the summons issued received back served upon the defendant on 22.11.2024. On the date fixed for hearing, no one appeared on behalf of the defendant and, thereafter, no written statement has been filed. Accordingly, the matter was proceeded ex-parte vide order of this Court dated 22.04.2025 and was listed for plaintiff's evidence. 3. In the meanwhile, the plaintiff bank substituted their AR to Mr. Anuj Kumar, Chief Manager, by way of an application. In order to substantiate their case, as delineated in the plaint, the plaintiff bank adduced the evidence of Mr. Anuj Kumar (Chief Manager), the AR of the plaintiff bank, as PW-1. PW-1 tendered his evidence by way of an affidavit, Exhibit PW-1/A, wherein Dated 20.11.2025 SHARMA 2025.11.20 16:26:29 +0530 he deposed on the same lines, as stated in the plaint and placed on record the true and correct copy of the Power of Attorney dated 29.10.2018 as Exhibit PW-1/1 (OSR) to show his authority to depose and give evidence on behalf of the plaintiff bank. He has also placed on record the true and correct copy of Board Resolution dated 14.11.2017, true and correct copy of deponent identity card and true and correct copy of Gazette Notification dated 02.01.2019 Bank Of Baroda vs Basanti Chaturvedi on 20 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46455642/ 3 regarding amalgamation of Vijaya Bank & Dena Bank with Bank of Baroda as Mark A, Mark B and Mark C respectively. It is stated in the said affidavit that the defendant approached the plaintiff bank for a loan of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only), by way of his application dated 30.12.2016, the original of which is placed on record as Exhibit PW-1/2. The defendant submitted the requisite documents with the plaintiff bank including self attested copy of PAN Card, original electricity bill, self attested copy of udyog aadhar memorandum, self attested copy of license issued by department of food safety which have been placed on record as Mark D, Exhibit PW1/3, Mark E and Mark F respectively. On submission of the said application of the defendant and documents, the plaintiff bank is stated to have sanctioned the loan of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) at an interest @ 9.65% per annum on floating basis with monthly rests , vide original sanction communication DOC 2-140, placed on record as Exhibit PW-1/4. The defendant then executed the original certificate of Loan papers (DOC54) , original loan agreement cum hypothecation deed DOC. 53 dated, original demand promissory note DOC.5 and original undertaking DOC 35 dated all 30.12.2016 in respect of the loan and the original of these documents have been placed on record as Exhibit PW-1/5, Exhibit PW-1/6, Exhibit PW-1/7 and Exhibit PW-1/8 respectively. The defendant is stated to have acknowledged the existing liability/debt as on 18.08.2021 of Rs.49,684.60/- (Rupees Forty-Nine Thousand Six Hundred Eighty-Four and Dated 20.11.2025 Bank of Baroda v. Basanti Chaturvedi Pg no.5/7 NIHARIKA KUMAR KUMAR Date: SHARMA 2025.11.20 16:26:39 +0530 Sixty Paisa Only) vide acknowledgment letter, which has been placed on record as Exhibit PW-1/10. It is alleged that the defendant defaulted in payment of the EMI/overdue amounts. To show the existing liability of the defendant, PW-1 has relied upon the statement of loan account of the defendant as maintained by the plaintiff bank. The statement of the loan account of the defendant with the upgradation sheet is placed on record as Exhibit PW-1/11 (Colly), which has been proved by PW-1 with the aid of the certificate issued in terms of Section 2A of the Bankers Books Evidence Act, 1891 which is also part of Exhibit PW-1/12 (Colly). 4. No other witness was examined by the plaintiff bank. The plaintiff's evidence was closed by way of a separate statement.
